root_cause_text: Deploy 249a1c2 (payments 1.9.1) set PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE=1.0, which turns on fraud screening for every charge. The fraud check code reads signals["risk_score"] (payments.py line 85) and that key is not there, so it raises an unhandled KeyError and /charge returns 500 on almost every request. I didn't confirm where the signals data comes from or why the key is missing.

recommended_action.reason: Payments' latest deploy (249a1c2) turned on a fraud-check code path that crashes with KeyError on almost every charge, and that failure spreads to orders and gateway. Rolling back to 1.9.0 (PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE=0.0) turns the failing code path off again.

root_cause_text: Deploy b37d34e (payments 1.9.1, 01:03:56Z) changed PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE from 0.0 to 0.3. When a charge is fraud-checked, payments.py line 85 reads signals['risk_score'], that key is missing, and the KeyError surfaces as an HTTP 500 from /charge. The errors then spread up through orders and gateway.

recommended_action.reason: Deploy b37d34e turned on the fraud-check code path, and every charge it handles crashes with KeyError: 'risk_score'. Rolling payments back to 1.9.0 sets PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE back to 0.0, which should stop the 500s in payments and in the services above it.

root_cause_text: Deploy db08160 (payments 1.9.1) set PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE=0.3, which sends about 30% of charges through run_fraud_check. That function reads signals["risk_score"] at payments.py line 85, and the key is missing, so it throws an unhandled KeyError and the request returns HTTP 500.

recommended_action.reason: Rolling back payments deploy db08160 restores PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE=0.0. That turns off the fraud check code path that throws KeyError 'risk_score', which is the only error source found, and orders and gateway should recover once payments does.

root_cause_text: Deploy a7c9d97 (orders 2.1.1, 'Keep all receipts in memory for faster re-downloads') set ORDERS_RECEIPT_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS=0, up from 50. The commit message says the intent was to keep all receipts, so 0 appears to mean no limit. The cache now keeps every receipt and orders memory grows with traffic.

recommended_action.reason: Rolling back orders deploy a7c9d97 brings back the 50-item receipt cache limit and stops memory from growing without bound. A restart alone would only clear memory for a while, and it would grow again.

root_cause_text: Deploy 1fd1f53 changed ORDERS_DB_POOL_MODE from per_request to persistent. Orders now keeps its Postgres connections open instead of releasing them. Postgres allows 40 connections with 3 reserved for admins, and orders is holding all 37 of the rest, so new connections are refused and requests fail with 500.

recommended_action.reason: Deploy 1fd1f53 switched orders to persistent DB connections, and those connections are not being returned, so Postgres has no free slots. Rolling back to 2.1.0 (per_request) restores the previous connection handling and frees the connections. A restart would only help until the connections leak again.

root_cause_text: The external payment provider started answering charges in about 1.5s from roughly 01:20:52. payments waits on it, so payments p95 rose to about 2s, and orders and gateway, which sit above it, slowed by at least the same amount. No deploy, flag change or restart of ours lines up with when it started.

recommended_action.reason: The slowness is in the external payment provider, which we don't operate, and none of our deploys or flag changes matches when it started. Escalate to the provider or payments-integration owner. Rolling back or restarting our services would not help.

root_cause_text: The external payment provider slowed down: each charge call now takes about 1.5s. Every payments /charge request waits on it, and the delay passes up through orders and gateway, pushing gateway p95 to about 1.97s.

recommended_action.reason: The latency comes from the external payment provider, where each charge takes about 1.5s. We don't operate the provider, so escalate to its owner or the vendor. Rolling back the orders deploy, which only changed the version number, or restarting a service would not help.

root_cause_text: Turning on checkout_v2_pricing (changed by growth-team at 2026-10-14T01:27:13Z) makes the gateway build order requests with amount_cents=0. orders' input validation rejects them with 422, and the gateway returns 502 for them. No deploy happened in this window: the only deploy is the initial release at 01:26:09Z, before the errors started. All containers are healthy with no restarts.

recommended_action.reason: The errors began right after this flag was turned on, and they come from the gateway sending amount_cents=0, which orders rejects. Setting the flag back to false should restore valid order amounts without needing a deploy.

root_cause_text: The growth team turned on checkout_v2_pricing (false to true) at 01:31:12Z, and the gateway now builds orders with amount_cents=0. Orders correctly rejects these as invalid (422 'Input should be greater than 0'), and the gateway returns 502 for each one. Nothing downstream is failing: payments and orders just stopped getting valid traffic.

recommended_action.reason: The errors began when this flag went from false to true, and since then the gateway has been sending amount_cents=0, which orders rejects. Setting it back to false follows the feature-flags runbook and requires no deploy.

root_cause_text: Deploy 7651fbf ('Move provider credentials to the secrets manager') deleted PAYMENTS_API_KEY from services/payments.env. When payments starts, it checks for the key, finds it missing, raises 'RuntimeError: PAYMENTS_API_KEY is not set' and exits with code 3, so it never comes up.

recommended_action.reason: Rolling back 7651fbf puts PAYMENTS_API_KEY back in payments.env, which should let payments start again. Re-apply the secrets-manager change only once the key can actually reach the container from the secrets manager.

root_cause_text: Deploy 32a47e3 (payments 1.9.1, labelled 'chore: sync config') raised PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE from 0.0 to 0.3. This switched on run_fraud_check, which reads signals["risk_score"] at payments.py line 85 and throws KeyError: 'risk_score'. Those requests get a 500 from payments. The error rate settled at about 30%, matching the 0.3 rate, though I did not confirm the setting means 'fraction of requests checked'. The 500s pass up through orders to gateway.

recommended_action.reason: Rolling back 32a47e3 sets PAYMENTS_FRAUD_CHECK_RATE back to 0.0. That should switch off the crashing fraud-check path and stop the roughly 30% 5xx rate in payments, orders and gateway.

root_cause_text: Deploy 727d5a8 (orders 2.1.1) set ORDERS_RECEIPT_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS=0 (was 50). After that restart the receipt cache has grown with no cap, and orders memory has grown along with it.

recommended_action.reason: Rolling back 727d5a8 puts ORDERS_RECEIPT_CACHE_MAX_ITEMS back to 50. That bounds the receipt cache and stops the memory growth. A restart alone would only reset memory until the cache refills.

root_cause_text: Deploy ba383dd switched ORDERS_DB_POOL_MODE to persistent. With that setting, orders keeps its database connections instead of returning them. It filled all 37 usable Postgres slots (max_connections=40, 3 reserved for admins), so new requests cannot connect and fail with psycopg OperationalError.

recommended_action.reason: Deploy ba383dd changed how orders handles database connections, and right after it orders filled every Postgres slot. Rolling back puts per_request mode back so connections get released. A restart alone would only free them until they fill up again.

root_cause_text: Deploy 663304f at 02:26:21Z deleted the line PAYMENTS_API_KEY from the payments release settings (services/payments.env). On startup, payments.py check_api_key() raises RuntimeError("PAYMENTS_API_KEY is not set; payments cannot reach the provider"), so the app exits with code 3 every time and restarts over and over.

recommended_action.reason: Rolling back deploy 663304f puts back the payments.env that contains PAYMENTS_API_KEY (version 1.9.0), so payments can start again. Restarting alone will not help, because the key is missing from the current release settings.
